--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.contract_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Contract two nodes by merging node\_2 into node\_1. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.contract_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Contract two nodes by merging node\_2 into node\_1. title: >- [Graph.contract_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Contract two nodes by merging node\_2 into node\_1. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Contract two nodes by merging `node_2` into `node_1`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L50196-L50317){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.contract_nodes( node_1, node_2, self_loops=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Contract nodes](../assets/graphs/contract-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph in two rows; node A is outlined as the survivor and node D, which is not adjacent to A, is in the accent color with its edge to E. After: D is gone, shown dashed, and its edge has been rerouted to A, so a new accent edge joins A and E." width="100%"} Creates a new graph where node `node_2` is removed and all its edges are redirected to node `node_1`. If there was an edge between `node_1` and `node_2`, it becomes a self-loop on `node_1` (unless `self_loops=False`). This operation does not modify the original graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to keep (node ID or label). All edges from `node_2` will be redirected here. [node_2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to merge into `node_1` (node ID or label). This node will be removed. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), edges between `node_1` and `node_2` become self-loops on `node_1`. If `False`, such edges are removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `node_2` contracted into `node_1`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `node_1` and `node_2` are the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Contraction is a fundamental graph-minor operation: the surviving node $u$ inherits every edge incident to $v$, and any $u$-$v$ edge becomes a self-loop on $u$ unless `self_loops=False` suppresses it. The traversal costs $O(E)$ time and produces a fresh graph, so the original is left intact. Node $u$ keeps its label and attributes, and edge weights carry through unchanged. Edges at $u$ that end up joining the same pair of nodes collapse into the first of them, which keeps its ID, weight and attributes, so $u$ is left with at most one edge to each neighbor (one in each direction on a directed graph) and at most one self-loop. Edges between other nodes, parallel ones included, are kept as they are. Contraction is what drives the aggregation phase of Louvain community detection and underpins the reduced graphs used in minor-based algorithms like planarity testing. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~contract_nodes_multi`) : Merge any number of nodes into one. [](`~contracted_edge`) : Merge the two endpoints of an existing edge. [](`~quotient_graph`) : Collapse every block of a partition at once. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Contracting "A" and "B" in the path "A -- B -- C -- D" keeps "A" and moves B's edges to it: ::: {#76ada52b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) merged = path.contract_nodes("A", "B") merged.has_node("B"), merged.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (False, ['A--A', 'A--C', 'C--D']) ``` ::: ::: The edge that joined them becomes a self-loop on "A" unless `self_loops=False`: ::: {#6904dff4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} merged = path.contract_nodes("A", "B", self_loops=False) merged.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A--C', 'C--D'] ``` ::: ::: ### The two leaders as one The karate club split between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33). Contracting the two into one node shows how far their reach goes together. The merged node keeps the instructor's label: ::: {#2a18ecc7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() leaders = karate.contract_nodes("0", "33") karate.get_degree("0"), karate.get_degree("33"), leaders.get_degree("0") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (16, 17, 29) ``` ::: ::: The instructor has 16 ties and the administrator 17, but the merged node has 29, not 33: 4 members are tied to both leaders, and their two ties merge into one. That leaves 3 members tied to neither, 16, 24 and 25: ::: {#7e8492f1 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} merged = leaders.get_id_from_label("0") reach = set(leaders.get_neighbors(merged)) | {merged} others = [n for n in leaders.get_node_ids() if n not in reach] sorted(leaders.get_label_from_id(n) for n in others) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['16', '24', '25'] ``` ::: ::: The merged node is highlighted with the three members it doesn't reach: ::: {#d86687a1 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} leaders.plot(label_by="label", highlight=["0", "16", "24", "25"], seed=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Transforming graphs](../user-guide/transforming.qmd#merging-nodes) merges the Tornabuoni into the Medici in the Florentine families network.
